extraction.name: PIQA
extraction.description: PIQA is a benchmark dataset for physical commonsense reasoning. Given a physical goal expressed in natural language, a model must choose the most sensible solution, testing whether language models can link text to an intuitive physics model of the world.
extraction.creator: Yonatan Bisk; Rowan Zellers; Ronan Le Bras; Jianfeng Gao; Yejin Choi
extraction.publisher: Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected by asking annotators to create goal-solution multiple-choice examples inspired by how-to instructions from Instructables. Annotators glanced at an instructable, used it as inspiration to construct a physical goal, wrote a valid solution, and then created an invalid permutation of their own solution.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Crowdsourced how-to instructions from instructables.com, including instructional content that annotators used as prompts or inspiration.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators were prompted with links to Instructables and asked to create goal-solution pairs: articulate a physical goal, write a valid solution, and provide a subtly invalid permutation ('trick'). Qualification HITs were used before the main task, and separate validation HITs were run afterward; low-agreement examples were removed and low-agreement annotators were de-qualified.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Validation was based on annotator agreement; examples with low agreement were removed, and users with low agreement were de-qualified. Qualification required >80% accuracy on identifying well-formed pairs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies reporting bias in language as a source of bias affecting physical commonsense knowledge, since such facts are rarely explicitly stated in text.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has some questionable labels or examples where the marked mistake may actually be correct and require external verification; additionally, the authors argue that learning physical knowledge from language alone is inherently limiting.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames physical commonsense reasoning as important for progress toward AI systems and robots that can interact with the world and understand natural language.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is introduced as a benchmark to evaluate language representations and natural language understanding models on physical commonsense reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Train, development, and test folds were automatically produced by AFLite to handle spurious biases and make the dataset adversarial to BERT.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For analysis, solution strings were tokenized, lowercased, and had punctuation removed before computing edit distance; for modeling, examples were truncated at 150 tokens.
